messages.schedule.archive.confirm: Archive this scheduled task? It won’t run automatically anymore, and its read permissions are revoked with it.
messages.schedule.directory.summary: Run scheduled conversation tasks and receive plugin reminders on time.
messages.schedule.form.help: When due, it runs a turn in this task’s own chat, not in an existing Coding session.
messages.schedule.form.instructions-hint: Read-only by default. File edits still go through the existing review queue.
messages.schedule.form.instructions-placeholder: Write what AI should check and report when this task is due…
messages.schedule.form.notify: Highlight in the list when an update is important
messages.schedule.form.once-hint: The time was set where this task was scheduled and can’t be changed here.
messages.schedule.form.reads: Once it’s created, choose here what it can read. Without a choice, it reads project files only.
messages.schedule.form.time-hint: Uses this computer’s local time. Alarms only fire while Molis Work is running.
messages.schedule.form.title: Title
messages.schedule.hint.model: No AI model is set up yet, so this task can’t run automatically when due. You can save it now and add a model in Settings › Models later.
messages.schedule.hint.workspace: This project has no folder linked yet, so AI can’t read project files when due. Save it now and add a folder in Project settings › Inputs and output later.
messages.schedule.job.identity-unverified: The original installation can’t be verified. Review the reminder and the current plugin before restoring it.
messages.schedule.job.install-first: Install and enable the corresponding plugin, then refresh to review it.
messages.schedule.list.empty-body: Schedule a time and AI will check and report back here automatically (read-only). Reminders created by other features also appear here.
messages.schedule.operation.changed: The task has changed. Return to the list and choose again.
messages.schedule.operation.gone: The original alarm or operation is missing. Keep the history and create a new schedule.
messages.schedule.operation.warning-resume: Assign the original operation and input to the current installation. Undispatched work waits for a fresh wakeup, then keeps the original interval. This confirmation allows plugin code to run.
messages.schedule.operation.warning-retry: The previous call may already have incurred costs or made external changes. Retrying runs the same input again and may duplicate those effects. Check the external records first.
messages.schedule.operation.warning-skip: Skip the earliest unknown occurrence without running it again. Review any remaining unknown outcomes, then continue at the original interval; a one-time task ends here.
messages.schedule.reads.created: Task created. Choose what it can read and the next run can use it.
messages.schedule.reads.failed: Can’t show what this task can read right now
messages.schedule.reads.failed-body: Permissions can’t be read right now. Try reading them again. The task checks again when due; if it still can’t read them, that run stops and reports why.
messages.schedule.reads.needs-confirmation: One category can read more, or reads differently now. It can’t be read until you confirm it again.
messages.schedule.reads.none: None chosen; reads project files only
messages.schedule.reads.nothing-readable: None of the chosen categories can be read right now. It still runs when due and reports what it couldn’t read.
messages.schedule.reads.removed: One category is no longer offered, so this task can’t read it.
messages.schedule.reads.title: Data it can read
messages.schedule.reads.unavailable: One category’s plugin is turned off, so it can’t be read for now. The permission stays and comes back when the plugin is re-enabled.
messages.schedule.reads.workspace: Tasks that read project files need a linked project folder first.
messages.schedule.recovery.gone: This reminder has already been restored or no longer exists. Return to the list to check.
messages.schedule.recovery.note: Keep the original schedule. An overdue reminder is delivered once, then repeats at the original interval. This doesn’t run plugin code.
messages.schedule.recovery.title: Restore this reminder
messages.schedule.agent-role.reader.name: Read-only runner
messages.schedule.agent-role.brief.name: Read data and run
messages.schedule.read-group.operations.descripti: This project’s scheduled tasks and reminders, plus other plugins’ scheduled operations with their original input
messages.schedule.read-group.operations.title: Scheduled operations
messages.schedule.read-group.reminders.descriptio: This project’s reminders: what they say (including reminders other plugins set), which plugin set them, and when they’re next due
messages.schedule.read-group.reminders.title: Reminders
messages.schedule.help.title: Schedule
messages.schedule.help.what: Runs a recurring task at the time you set, saving results back to this project and sending externally only to recipients you named.
messages.schedule.help.example-1: Every Monday morning, turn meeting notes into a project report
messages.schedule.help.example-2: Every evening, summarize items waiting for your reply
messages.schedule.help.scope: Runs strictly within the permissions you granted and is billed by your model provider; pausing or revoking stops the next run and states why.
messages.schedule.help.advanced-summary: Time zone, missed runs, and pausing
messages.schedule.help.advanced: Uses this computer’s time zone; if the computer was asleep, it runs once on waking rather than replaying every missed slot.
